title: Hanuma's search for Seetha
introduction: Hanuma's search for Seetha, together with Angada and others is started. They search certain mountains and forests belonging to Vindhya, but in vain. They enter many uninhabited forests and places. Angada kills a demon presuming him to be Ravana. Their hearts sadden when their search became futile at these places.
closing: इति वाल्मीकि रामायणे आदि काव्ये किष्किन्ध काण्डे अष्ट चत्वारिंशः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 48th chapter in Kishkindha Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
सह तार अंगदाभ्याम् तु सहसा हनुमान् कपिः |
सुग्रीवेण यथा उद्दिष्टम् तम् देशम् उपचक्रमे
verses.iast:
saha tāra aṃgadābhyām tu sahasā hanumān kapiḥ |
sugrīveṇa yathā uddiṣṭam tam deśam upacakrame
verses.translation: Hanuma, the monkey, quickly started along with Angada, Lt. Tara, and others to that province which Sugreeva has indicated, namely the south.

glosses.meaning: Lt. Tara, Angada and others, along with
that, province, [to go to,] started out.

verses.devanagari:
स तु दूरम् उपागम्य सर्वैः तैः कपि सत्तमैः |
ततो विचित्य विन्ध्यस्य गुहाः च गहनानि च
पर्वताग्र नदी दुर्गान् सरांसि विपुल द्रुमान् |
वृक्ष खण्डान् च विविधान् पर्वतान् वन पादपान्
verses.iast:
sa tu dūram upāgamya sarvaiḥ taiḥ kapi sattamaiḥ |
tato vicitya vindhyasya guhāḥ ca gahanāni ca
parvatāgra nadī durgān sarāṃsi vipula drumān |
vṛkṣa khaṇḍān ca vividhān parvatān vana pādapān
verses.translation: Arriving at a remote place with all of those powerful monkeys, then Hanuma searched the caves and forests of Vindhya Mountains, and on their mountaintops, at impassable places, at rivers and lakes, and in stands of trees with beamy trees, also on diverse mountains, forests and trees.

glosses.meaning: with all, of them, monkey, powerful ones
Vindhya mountain's, caves, also, forests, also
wide, trees, trees, stands of, also - forest areas having beamy trees

verses.devanagari:
अन्वेषमाणाः ते सर्वे वानराः सर्वतो दिशम् |
न सीताम् ददृशुर् वीरा मैथिलीम् जनक आत्मजाम्
verses.iast:
anveṣamāṇāḥ te sarve vānarāḥ sarvato diśam |
na sītām dadṛśur vīrā maithilīm janaka ātmajām
verses.translation: Though all of those brave vanara-s have searched in all directions they have not noticed the princess of Mithila and the daughter of Janaka, namely Seetha.

verses.devanagari:
ते भक्षयन्तो मूलानि फलानि विविधानि अपि |
अन्वेषमाणा दुर्धर्षा न्यवसन् तत्र तत्र ह
verses.iast:
te bhakṣayanto mūlāni phalāni vividhāni api |
anveṣamāṇā durdharṣā nyavasan tatra tatra ha
verses.translation: Feeding upon unalike fruits and tubers, sojourning here and there, those invulnerable vanara-s conducted their search.

verses.devanagari:
स तु देशो दुर्अन्वेषो गुहा गहनवान् महान् |
निर्जलम् निर्जनम् शून्यम् गहनम् घोर दर्शनम्
verses.iast:
sa tu deśo dur.hanveṣo guhā gahanavān mahān |
nirjalam nirjanam śūnyam gahanam ghora darśanam
verses.translation: But that province is an inscrutable one, deeply caved, deeply forested, much less of water and still less of people, a void and an impenetrable one with a ghastly look.

glosses.meaning: that, great, province, on its part

verses.devanagari:
ता दृशानि अन्या अपि अरण्यानि विचित्य भृइश पीडिताः |
स देशः च दुर्अन्वेष्यो गुहा गहनवान् महान्
verses.iast:
tā dṛśāni anyā api araṇyāni vicitya bhṛiśa pīḍitāḥ |
sa deśaḥ ca dur.hanveṣyo guhā gahanavān mahān
verses.translation: They are highly tormented when they vainly searched there, and even in another province that is also of the same kind, waterless and people-less, and an unreachable one, abstrusely caved and forested.

verses.devanagari:
त्यक्त्वा तु तम् ततः देशम् सर्वे वै हरि यूथपाः |
देशम् अन्यम् दुराधर्षम् विविशुः च अकुतो भयाः
verses.iast:
tyak{}tvā tu tam tataḥ deśam sarve vai hari yūthapāḥ |
deśam anyam durādhar.hṣam viviśuḥ ca akuto bhayāḥ
verses.translation: Then all of those monkey commanders gave up that province and entered another impermeable province as they are fearless from any quarter.

verses.devanagari:
यत्र वन्ध्य फला वृक्षा विपुष्पाः पर्ण वर्जिताः |
निस्तोयाः सरितो यत्र मूलम् यत्र सुदुर्लभम्
verses.iast:
yatra vandhya phalā vṛkṣā vipuṣpāḥ parṇa varjitāḥ |
nistoyāḥ sarito yatra mūlam yatra sudurlabham
verses.translation: Whereat the trees are infertile for fruiting, destitute of leaves and flowers, and whereat the brooks are deprived of waters, and whereat it is highly impossible to get even tubers, there they entered.

glosses.meaning: trees, with infertile, fruits - fruitless trees
brooks nis toyaaH = deprived of, waters

verses.devanagari:
न सन्ति महिषा यत्र न मृगा न च हस्तिनः |
शार्दूलाः पक्षिणो वा अपि ये च अन्ये वन गोचराः
verses.iast:
na santi mahiṣā yatra na mṛgā na ca hastinaḥ |
śārdūlāḥ pakṣiṇo vā api ye ca anye vana gocarāḥ
verses.translation: Where there are no buffalos, no elephants, no animals, nor even birds or tigers, or no other forest moving beings are there, for they do not have their feed there, they entered such a province.

verses.devanagari:
न च अत्र वृक्षा न ओषध्यो न वल्ल्यो न अपि वीरुधः |
स्निग्ध पत्राः स्थले यत्र पद्मिन्यः फुल्ल पंकजाः
प्रेक्षणीयाः सुगन्धाः च भ्रमरैः च वर्जिताः |
verses.iast:
na ca atra vṛkśā na oṣadhyo na vallyo na api vīrudhaḥ |
snigdha patrāḥ sthale yatra padminyaḥ phulla paṃkajāḥ
prekṣaṇīyāḥ sugandhāḥ ca bhramaraiḥ ca varjitāḥ |
verses.translation: Where there are no useful trees, nor herbal plants, nor climbing plants on trees, nor creeping plants on earth, and lotus-lakes which will be normally pleasing for sight have no soft leaves, nor bloomed lotuses on their creepers, and even honeybees are discarding them as they are not richly fragranced, in such a province those vanara-s have entered.

glosses.meaning: bloomed, from mud, birthed [lotuses birthed in lakes]

verses.devanagari:
कण्डुर् नाम महाभागः सत्य वादी तपो धनः
महर्षिः परम अमर्षी नियमैः दुष्प्रधर्षणः |
verses.iast:
kaṇḍur nāma mahābhāgaḥ satya vādī tapo dhanaḥ
maharṣiḥ parama amar.hṣī niyamaiḥ duṣ.hpradhar.hṣaṇaḥ |
verses.translation: A highly fortunate, veracious, ascetically wealthy sage known as Kandu is there in that province, and that great sage is a highly short-tempered, and an impossible one to subjugate by virtue of his own self-discipline.

verses.devanagari:
तस्य तस्मिन् वने पुत्रो बालको दश वार्षिकः
प्रणष्टो जीवित अन्ताय क्रुद्धः तेन महामुनिः |
verses.iast:
tasya tasmin vane putro bālako daśa vārṣikaḥ
praṇaṣṭo jīvita antāya kruddhaḥ tena mahāmuniḥ |
verses.translation: In that forest that sage lost his son, a ten-year-old boy, as that boy's life ended there by which that great sage is infuriated.

glosses.meaning: by the end of, lost, life [boy]

verses.devanagari:
तेन धर्माअत्मना शप्तम् कृत्स्नम् तत्र महद् वनम्
अशरण्यम् दुराधर्षम् मृग पक्षि विवर्जितम् |
verses.iast:
tena dharmāatmanā śaptam kṛtsnam tatra mahad vanam
aśaraṇyam durādharṣam mṛga pakṣi vivarjitam |
verses.translation: Thereby that virtue-souled sage cursed that great forest in it entirety to become an uninhabitable and impermeable forest abandoned by birds and animals.

glosses.meaning: by him, by that virtue-souled one, cursed.

verses.devanagari:
तस्य ते कानन अन्तान् तु गिरीणाम् कन्दराणि च
प्रभवाणि नदीनाम् च विचिन्वन्ति समाहिताः |
verses.iast:
tasya te kānana antān tu girīṇām kandarāṇi ca
prabhavāṇi nadīnām ca vicinvanti samāhitāḥ |
verses.translation: But those monkeys conscientiously searched such a forest up to its fringes, including its mountains, caves, fountains, and rivers.

glosses.meaning: forest, up to its fringes, but

verses.devanagari:
तत्र च अपि महात्मानो न अपश्यन् जनक आत्मजाम्
हर्तारम् रावणम् वा अपि सुग्रीव प्रिय कारिणः |
verses.iast:
tatra ca api mahātmāno na apaśyan janaka ātmajām
hartāram rāvaṇam vā api sugrīva priya kāriṇaḥ |
verses.translation: But not finding the daughter of Janaka or even her kidnapper Ravana there, those monkeys who are the perfecters of that which is acceptable to Sugreeva, have entered another fearsome forest.

glosses.meaning: to Sugreeva, acceptable deeds, perfecters of

verses.devanagari:
ते प्रविश्य तु तम् भीमम् लता गुल्म समावृतम्
ददृशुः भीम कर्माणम् असुरम् सुर निर्भयम् |
verses.iast:
te praviśya tu tam bhīmam latā gulma samāvṛtam
dadṛśuḥ bhīma karmāṇam asuram sura nirbhayam |
verses.translation: On entering another fearsome forest which is overly encompassed with climbers and shrubberies they saw a demon of fiendish deeds who is fearless of gods.

glosses.meaning: with climbers, shrubberies, overly encompassed with

verses.devanagari:
तम् दृष्ट्वा वनरा घोरम् स्थितम् शैलम् इव असुरम्
गाढम् परिहिताः सर्वे दृष्ट्वा तम् पर्वत उपमम् |
verses.iast:
tam dṛṣṭvā vanarā ghoram sthitam śailam iva asuram
gāḍham parihitāḥ sarve dṛṣṭvā tam parvata upamam |
verses.translation: All of those vanara-s are amazed to see that fiendish demon standing similar to a mountainous boulder, and apprehending an imminent danger on observing that mountain similar demon, those vanara-s have tightly girthed their wrestler's girdle-cloth.

glosses.meaning: fiendish, him, at demon, on seeing
tightly, around, girthed - their wrestler's girdle-cloth.

verses.devanagari:
सो अपि तान् वानरान् सर्वान् नष्टाः स्थ इति अब्रवीत् बली
अभ्यधावत सम्क्रुद्धो मुष्टिम् उद्यम्य संगतम् |
verses.iast:
so api tān vānarān sarvān naṣṭāḥ stha iti abravīt balī
abhyadhāvata samkruddho muṣṭim udyamya saṅgatam |
verses.translation: Even that mighty demon shouting at all vanara-s, 'you are all dead... stay,' rushed towards them shoving up his clenched fist.

glosses.meaning: to them, to all vanara-s, said - shouting

verses.devanagari:
तम् आपतन्तम् सहसा वालि पुत्रो अंगदः तदा
रावणो अयम् इति ज्ञात्वा तलेन अभिजघान ह |
verses.iast:
tam āpatantam sahasā vāli putro aṃgadaḥ tadā
rāvaṇo ayam iti jñātvā talena abhijaghāna ha |
verses.translation: Angada, the son of Vali, then presumed him who is onrushing as Ravana and saying, 'he is Ravana...' he quickly thwacked that demon indeed with his palm.

glosses.meaning: quickly, with his palm, thwacked, indeed.

verses.devanagari:
स वालि पुत्र अभिहतो वक्त्रात् शोणितम् उद्वमन्
असुरो न्यपतत् भूमौ पर्यस्त इव पर्वतः |
verses.iast:
sa vāli putra abhihato vak{}trāt śoṇitam udvaman
asuro nyapatat bhūmau paryasta iva parvataḥ |
verses.translation: When Vali's son whacked him that demon spewed forth blood from his throat and fell onto ground alike an inverted mountain.

glosses.meaning: by Vali's, son, one who is whacked
from throat, blood, up spewed [spewed forth]

verses.devanagari:
ते तु तस्मिन् निर् उच्छ्वासे वानरा जित काशिनः
व्यचिन्वन् प्रायशः तत्र सर्वम् तत् गिरि गह्वरम् |
verses.iast:
te tu tasmin nir ucchvāse vānarā jita kāśinaḥ
vyacinvan prāyaśaḥ tatra sarvam tat giri gahvaram |
verses.translation: When that demon breathed his last all of those monkeys with triumphal shimmer have wellnigh searched everywhere, and even in that cave of that mountain where that demon appeared, presuming that cave belonged to Ravana.

glosses.meaning: all, that [demon's,] mountain, cave, they searched.

verses.devanagari:
विचितम् तु ततः सर्वम् सर्वे ते कानन ओकसः
अन्यत् एव अपरम् घोरम् विविशुर् गिरि गह्वरम् |
verses.iast:
vicitam tu tataḥ sarvam sarve te kānana okasaḥ
anyat eva aparam ghoram viviśur giri gahvaram |
verses.translation: Then all those forest dwelling monkeys searched everywhere else, and like that they entered another horrible cave which is nearby.

glosses.meaning: all, those, forest, as their dwelling - monkeys

verses.devanagari:
ते विचित्य पुनः खिन्ना विनिष्पत्य समागताः |
एकांते वृक्ष मूले तु निषेदुर् दीन मानसाः
verses.iast:
te vicitya punaḥ khinnā viniṣpatya samāgatāḥ |
ekāṃte vṛkṣa mūle tu niṣedur dīna mānasāḥ
verses.translation: On searching that cave they came out saddened as their search is futile, and coming together they sat down at the base of a lonely tree downheartedly as their efforts are unsuccessful in searching Seetha.

glosses.meaning: at a lonely, tree, at its base
